clue.text: Light reading? Usually anything but!

parts.note: light here means lit up with gold and colour, so the reading matter is decorated pages; yet such handwritten medieval books are weighty, scholarly texts, hardly light reading in the casual sense

explanation.walkthrough: 'Light reading' looks like a beach novel, but 'light' is the decoration in gold leaf on hand-copied medieval books, which are anything but light in content.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand-copied medieval books decorated with gold and coloured pictures are said to be lit up, a pun on light reading.

clue.text: I arranged things close at hand

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the word things are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tidies the objects lying nearest to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges THINGS into NSIGHT, which follows I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something visible nearby is within view, so it is near enough to be seen.

clue.text: The pride of British rugby

parts.note: a pride is a group of big cats, and the touring rugby side drawn from Britain and Ireland is named after those big cats

explanation.walkthrough: The touring rugby team of Britain and Ireland is named after big cats, and a group of those cats is called a pride.
explanation.definitionFit: The British and Irish touring rugby union team bears this big-cat name, and a pride is the group noun for them.

clue.text: Drove doctor to meet cardinal

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
cardinal red is the scarlet of a cardinal's robes

explanation.surface: A physician travelled by car to an appointment with a senior churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: To have driven a vehicle is to have travelled by motor car.

clue.text: Token refusal by Milan assembly

parts.note: no is a word of refusal

indicators.note: assembly means the letters of Milan are put together again in a different order

explanation.surface: A city council in Italy makes a merely symbolic gesture of saying no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' rearranges MILAN into MINAL, placed after NO.
explanation.definitionFit: A token payment or gesture is one in name only, a small symbolic amount.

clue.text: Scoffing when the pleats are stitched down

definitions.meaning: to scoff is to eat greedily, as one does when tucking into a meal

definitions.text: when the pleats are stitched down
definitions.meaning: a tuck is a stitched fold, so folding pleats and sewing them in place is putting tucks in

explanation.definitionFit: Eating heartily and sewing folds into fabric are both described by this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Attorneys first employed by unconventional artist

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney in the US, so two attorneys give DA twice
first is abbreviated 1ST, with the numeral 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Lawyers were the first people a maverick painter ever hired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attorneys' is plural, so DA appears twice; 'first' written as 1st gives IST. 'employed by' simply links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dada was an early twentieth-century anti-art movement, so its followers were deliberately unconventional artists.

clue.text: Attempt by Birmingham MP to be overfrugal

parts.note: a go is an attempt or try
Clare Short was the Labour MP for Birmingham Ladywood

explanation.surface: A politician from Birmingham tries to cut spending too far.
explanation.walkthrough: Clare Short was a well-known Labour MP for Birmingham Ladywood and a cabinet minister in the 1990s and 2000s.
explanation.definitionFit: To go without enough of something through saving too much is to be stingy with oneself.

clue.text: Go to work! Understand? Excellent!

parts.note: to get a joke is to understand it
cracking is British slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A boss barks orders and checks that the staff follow.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal command to start working briskly and without delay.

clue.text: Graduate accountant confronts mother on the road

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate
a CA is a chartered accountant
a dam is the mother of an animal

explanation.surface: A university graduate meets an accountant and argues with their mother while travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confronts' and 'on' just place the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Crushed stone bound in layers forms a road surface named after its Scottish inventor McAdam.

clue.text: See 1 across
European banker is to monitor you and me

parts.note: to tag an offender electronically is to monitor them
us means you and me together

explanation.surface: A Continental financier plans to keep watch over the two of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is crossword code for a river, which has banks; the Tagus flows through Spain and Portugal to Lisbon.
explanation.definitionFit: This river of Spain and Portugal is a European waterway, and rivers have banks.

clue.text: Princess absorbed by model tenor in performance

indicators.note: absorbed by means the princess is taken inside the other letters
model as a verb means shape, so the letters of tenor in are reshaped

parts.note: Di is the familiar name of Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A princess is captivated by a fashion-model singer during a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' rearranges TENOR IN into RENTION, and 'absorbed by' places DI inside it after REN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendering of a song or play is a performance of it.

clue.text: Hit the sack when given the sack?

definitions.meaning: to hit the sack is slang for going to bed
someone made to leave work has stopped working, though by force rather than choice, hence the question mark

explanation.definitionFit: Going to bed and leaving one's job for good are both expressed by this past-tense verb.

clue.text: Angry US naval officer shows the flag

parts.note: seeing red, red-faced, means angry
an ensign is the lowest commissioned rank in the US Navy

explanation.surface: A furious American sailor displays the colours.
explanation.walkthrough: The Red Ensign is the flag flown by British merchant ships.
explanation.definitionFit: The British merchant navy flag is a red banner with the Union Jack in one corner.

clue.text: Emissaries support a faction in retreat

parts.note: a leg is a support, as on a table

indicators.note: in retreat means the word for faction goes backwards

parts.note: a set is a group or faction

explanation.surface: Envoys back a breakaway group as it withdraws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns SET into TES, after LEG and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Papal envoys are representatives sent on a mission abroad.

clue.text: Defensive position results from unusual dialect

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of dialect come out in a strange order

explanation.surface: A fortified stronghold is the product of an odd regional accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges DIALECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortress guarding a city is a strongly held position.

clue.text: More stingy when more intoxicated

definitions.meaning: tight means mean with money, so this is the comparative
tight is also slang for drunk

explanation.definitionFit: Tight means both mean with money and drunk; the comparative serves for both.

clue.text: Wood producers need large spanners

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
arches span gaps, so they are spanners

explanation.surface: Carpenters require big wrenches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spanners' looks like tools, but means things that span, as arches do over a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: These conifers yield timber, so they produce wood.

clue.text: Statesman gives sermon about international coalition

indicators.note: about means the abbreviation for sermon goes around the alliance

parts.note: ser. is an abbreviation of sermon
NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, an international alliance

explanation.surface: A politician preaches about the Western military alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SER round NATO, giving SE-NATO-R.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a senate is a legislator, a political figure.

clue.text: Serviceman flogged? That's right

parts.note: to flog is British slang for sell, so flogged means sold
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A soldier is whipped as punishment, and a bystander says it is fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flogged' suggests a whipping, but in British slang to flog is to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of an army is a man or woman in the armed services.

clue.text: It isn't Edward being corrupted

parts.note: 'tain't is a dialect contraction of it isn't
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Someone protests that Edward is not being led astray.
explanation.walkthrough: ''Tain't' is folksy shorthand for 'it isn't'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spoiled or polluted has been made impure.

clue.text: Usually popular with military big wig

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: A top army officer is well liked, as a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: As a general rule means on most occasions, as is normally the case.

clue.text: Book left by one member of reactionary views

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for a person of such views, the cartoon colonel who embodies them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A book abandoned by a right-wing politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Blimp, a 1930s British cartoon figure, stands for pompous reactionary opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon Colonel Blimp gave his name to any pompous diehard conservative.

clue.text: African bishop ordered tuna

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of tuna are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A churchman asks for fish at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like placing a restaurant order, but rearranges TUNA into ANTU.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bantu peoples form a large language family of central and southern Africa.

clue.text: Make a bomb

parts.note: to make a bomb is British slang for earning a fortune, not building an explosive device

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a 'bomb' is a large sum of money, so making one means earning a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Earning a great deal of money quickly is becoming wealthy.

clue.text: Fires singe terribly without it

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the jumbled letters go round the word it
terribly means the letters of singe are jumbled badly

explanation.surface: Fire scorches badly when it is absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: 'terribly' rearranges SINGE into IGNES, which goes round IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something alight is to start it burning.

clue.text: Encircles circles with a circle

parts.note: rings are circles
a round is a circle

explanation.surface: A ring of rings round another loop.
explanation.definitionFit: To surround something is to put a ring round it; the idiom also means to outdo easily.
